[b]Real Training Script Launched[/b]

This script offers 10 times the regular points. The script will randomly select a starting point between 2011 and 2020. Historical data will be scaled to become ETF prices, so players cannot determine the exact historical position of the index based on ETF prices. This script provides all the index ETFs available in this game, so there's no need to specifically choose real data to use.

notes.title: Real data
notes.notes:
[b]This update adds 700M of content, mainly consisting of real data including the following:[/b]

NASDAQ-100 
S&P 500 
Dow Jones Index
Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index
Shenzhen Stock Exchange Component Index 
Hang Seng Index 
Nikkei 225 
TWII

[b]The index content comprises 1-minute data spanning approximately 20 years[/b]

[b]Application of Real Data[/b] 

Currently, the intraday trading curves have been replaced with real data, meaning the intraday curves now represent historical, authentic data. However, the data is not directly utilized but processed to align with current market conditions.

[b]Changes to Intraday Trading[/b] 

The simulation of intraday trading has been modified. Now, the goal of the simulation is to follow the guidance of real data. Given the incorporation of real data, plans are also underway to relax the rules for intraday trading in the future. Since it's real data, the immense wealth gained by players in intraday trading should be attributed to their individual abilities rather than game exploits.

[b]How to Set Real Data[/b] 

Real data is automatically set upon selecting a language. Currently, three languages are available: Selecting Simplified Chinese will default to the Shanghai Stock Exchange Composite Index Selecting Traditional Chinese will default to Taiwan Weighted Index Selecting English will default to S&P 500

Alternatively, you can set other data in the confirmation interface upon entering the game.

[b]Update Plan[/b] 

Next, I will introduce a training mode and intelligent trading functions based on real data, turning this game into a tool that can provide practical strategy training.

notes.title: Fixed
notes.notes:
Fixed the issue that the industry interface did not display English. Fixed the issue that some Chinese characters could not be displayed.

Reworked the company details interface (access is by clicking on the company name in the upper left corner of the trading interface). Added an events page to the company details interface. Reworked the news page of the company details interface.

Now let's talk about how your stock trading went this month. I had a premonition before the Nasdaq crash, so I liquidated my positions in advance. But my greedy nature led me to increase my position by 15% at the peak, and the next day's plunge taught me a lesson. When the Nasdaq fell by 10%, I entered the market again to buy at the bottom (25% position), but suffered another sharp decline the next day. Nasdaq adjustments are common, but why did I feel that this time was different? Because the rise was too fast, exceeding the growth rate of fundamentals, and coupled with the arrival of an important time node, the bubble was likely to burst at this time. However, I won't wait for the bubble to burst completely before entering the market, because I don't know when the bottom will be. I started to gradually increase my positions according to my plan. I made a lot of mistakes this time, but fortunately, I always maintained a safe position and did not suffer fatal damage.

notes.title: What have I been doing recently
notes.notes:
It's been about a month since I last updated this game. 
What have I been doing? Nothing much.
 The Nasdaq crashed, and for the past month, I've been stuck in a cycle of selling stocks, trying to buy low, cutting my losses, and then trying to buy low again. I feel exhausted. Every time I open VS and see the code, all I want to do is sleep.

But, I've finally broken free from that cycle. I've set up a regular investment plan, and I'm going to continue updating this game. 
Sorry for the delay.

notes.title: Partial Function Adjustments and Fixes
notes.notes:
[b]Expert Functionality Offline[/b]
The expert functionality seemed not very useful, so it has been taken offline. Its original position has been replaced by the industry feature.

[b]Industry Interface[/b]
In the industry interface, you can view prices of industry goods. Clicking on a specific industry will bring up detailed information about it. You can also see the prosperity of the industry and the companies it contains here.

[b]Company Behavior: Stock Buyback Added[/b]
Previously, when a company had excess money, it would choose to pay dividends or expand. Now, the functionality of stock buybacks has been added. Buying back stocks reduces the circulating shares and can increase the company's stock price valuation.

[b]Adjustment to Company Expansion Behavior[/b]
Thresholds for company expansion behavior have been adjusted. Now, companies will be more cautious when expanding. Expansion may involve issuing more stocks and taking out loans.

[b]Company Behavior: Contraction Added[/b]
In cases where there is industry contraction or when a company is at a competitive disadvantage, leading to overcapacity, the company will contract. This involves selling surplus assets to raise funds and reduce maintenance costs.

[b]Regarding Delisting[/b]
If a company's stock price remains below 1 yuan for 10 consecutive days, the company will be delisted. However, delisting is currently unlikely to occur quickly because no companies were initially set up to approach delisting, and the process from weakening to delisting would be lengthy.

[b]Information Prompting for Company Behavior[/b]
Information prompting for company behavior is not yet complete and is planned to be completed next week.

[b]Company Information Access[/b]
Clicking on the company name in the upper left corner of the trading interface will bring up a window with specific information about the company. You can view the company's competitiveness and its competitors in the industry.

notes.title: Preview:Rise and Fall
notes.notes:
Firstly, I don't particularly like doing previews; I prefer to release content once it's completed.
So.... I'm unable to update to a new version this week, let me explain why.

[b]Industry Prosperity Value[/b]
The industry will have a prosperity value attribute, with 100 being the baseline. Values above 100 will boost industry profits and market capacity, while values below 100 will do the opposite.

[b]Prosperity Rate[/b]
Every quarter consists of thirty days, and each day a coin is tossed to determine the prosperity value for that day. The accumulation over thirty days will be settled on the 30th day.

[b]Company Profit[/b]
Company profit = Users * Product price * Profit margin - Company maintenance cost

[b]Company Users[/b]
Users are the most important asset for a company. Every quarter, a portion of the company's users will churn, which is related to the industry's "stickiness."
The churned segment will be contested by competitors within the same industry.

[b]Company Valuation[/b]
Company valuation has been revamped, varying slightly across different industries. Superior companies will have higher valuations.

I've made changes to the core logic of the game, and these days I’ve been debugging these functions.
These significant modifications are not compatible with the current script, so I need to revise the script as well.
This is why I can't release a new version this week; I need to revise the script, and it's a substantial amount of work.

[b]Regarding the Flaws of the New Interface[/b]
The new trading interface may not have as complete functionality as the old one, and it may not be as reliable, also containing some bugs.
I apologize for the issues and will continue to optimize the interface.

[b]Regarding Experience Optimization[/b]
This is also in the plan; I need time to solve these issues one by one. I hope for your understanding and patience.

notes.title: Retail vs.Wall Street is updated in the demo
notes.notes:
The event content is updated  in the Demo.

Event types include: Monster Stocks, Bullish/Bearish Indices, Bullish/Bearish Individual Stocks, Retail Investors vs. Wall Street.

Events go through stages: Incubation, Mild, Furious, Dissipation, Calm, and End, with each stage having different levels of impact. Effective impact stages are Mild, Furious, and Dissipation.

Events are rated by impact: D < C < B < A < S. The higher the rating, the greater the impact. However, events do not solely determine stock trends; they are influenced by other factors too.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44873682/5a7a08800f996bbb27d7f87c562d5de3679c6268.png[/img]

In the Retail Investors vs. Wall Street event, players act as retail investors and can participate, influencing the outcome. Player actions such as buying or selling stocks affect their influence. The player's influence opposes Wall Street's influence, affecting stock trends. The player's influence ranges from -0.1 to 0.1, depending on their trading volume during the event. Player influence is rated accordingly: Traitor, Deadweight, Neutral, Backbone, or Pillar.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44873682/af672010b17bb9366518bbb7dc2729332e09fbc0.png[/img]

The main tasks ahead:

Design a feature allowing players to initiate events themselves, including event levels and activation conditions.
Improve event statistics and summarization, allowing players to easily preview their impact and profits during events.

Additionally, the Demo will be closed or discontinued after the game is released, as I don't want to maintain two different versions.

notes.title: Online Plan and Recent Work Progress
notes.notes:
The past few weeks have been tough for me because my dog fell ill, and I needed to take care of him.

The game is scheduled to launch on June 7th. Currently, the focus is on optimizing performance, fixing bugs, and developing auxiliary features.

Here is the recent work completed:

Single-session saving. If a game session becomes too long and you wish to interrupt the game, you can exit the game, and the current session will be saved. The next time you log in, the previous session will automatically load. The game's saving and loading follow a "read and burn" mode. Once loaded, the save file will be deleted, and exiting the game will overwrite the save file. This is to prevent altering the future through save/load manipulation.

Added guidance. This includes an overview of the game and beginner tutorials.
